feature.title: Durable offline-first sync (A5) plus explicit conflict handling (A6)
feature.summary: Turn the M2 single-user sync core into a durable offline-first system with explicit conflict handling: bounded retries that stop, a manual Retry sync, outbox durability across process reconstruction, lost-wakeup protection on the single serialized pipeline, reconnect resumption, safe minimal outbox coalescing; and a persisted conflict record with explicit title/body resolution (Keep Local / Keep Server / Keep Both with a NEW client UUID), item-level checklist merge, operation-ordered labels, server-authority metadata, explicit delete-vs-edit, a 7-day product Trash retention that is structurally distinct from the sync tombstone, and tombstone anti-resurrection with tombstone GC disabled.

purpose: This package is a TEMPORARY EXECUTION CONTRACT covering the whole M3 milestone (A5 + A6). It exists so that a later fresh session can implement A5 and then A6 through the SAME unmodified Contract Guard, under an explicit and bounded write surface, with A5 kept as a light checkpoint inside ONE session and ONE final verification pass. This contract-creation task performed targeted discovery and authored the package; it does not implement M3.

There is one unique pipeline and one enqueuer seam (UniqueWorkEnqueuer). There is no backoff criteria, no per-mutation attempt bound, no drain-until-stable and no persisted request generation.
android_sync_engine.lost_wakeup_risk: With ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP a trigger that arrives while a run is active is dropped by WorkManager. Today the drop is harmless only because the engine pushes ALL pending outbox rows in the run it is already doing. A5 must PROVE this property (or add the smallest correct mechanism) rather than assume it.
android_sync_engine.trigger: data/sync/SyncTrigger.kt — fun interface SyncTrigger { fun requestSync() } plus NoopSyncTrigger
android_sync_engine.conflict_today: A 409 sets the ENTITY to SyncState.CONFLICT and DELETES the outbox row. There is NO persisted conflict record, no local/remote payload capture, no conflict type, no resolution state, and no conflict UI. The backend 409 carries only { error: REVISION_CONFLICT } with NO current revision and NO current server payload, so a client cannot resolve a conflict from the response alone.

target_architecture.diagram: Android (Room SSOT + persisted outbox + persisted conflict records) --(HTTP, unique note_sync pipeline)--> KeepLab Backend (server revision authority + change log + tombstones) --(JDBC)--> PostgreSQL
target_architecture.android_side: Room stays the local SSOT. The persisted Room outbox is the authority for pending work (never an in-memory list). One serialized `note_sync` pipeline. A5 adds bounded retry, manual retry, outbox durability, lost-wakeup protection, reconnect and safe coalescing. A6 adds a persisted conflict record, explicit resolution (Keep Local / Keep Server / Keep Both), item-level checklist merge, operation-ordered labels, server-authority metadata, explicit delete-vs-edit, and a 7-day product Trash distinct from the sync tombstone.
target_architecture.backend_side: The server stays the single revision/order authority. M3 extends the sync schema only as required (conflict response payload carrying the current authoritative revision and current server state, Trash timestamp handling, final-delete/tombstone handling, change-log semantics as required). No attachments, no object storage, no collaboration, no multi-device feature, no push.

requirements.statement: A small explicit error/retry classification exists (AUTH_REQUIRED, CONFLICT, TEMPORARY_RETRYABLE, PERMANENT_VALIDATION_FAILURE, NOT_FOUND_NON_DESTRUCTIVE, SUCCESS); transport failure, HTTP 429, generic 5xx and a temporary refresh/network condition are TEMPORARY_RETRYABLE and are never marked permanent by default, while validation/permanent failures are not retried forever.
Retries are bounded with simple recorded constants (AUTO_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS, BACKOFF_POLICY, BACKOFF_INITIAL_DELAY, BACKOFF_MAX_DELAY) and automatic retries eventually stop.
After retry exhaustion the entity and its outbox row remain durable, the sync state becomes SYNC_FAILED, manual retry becomes available and no local data is deleted.

One simple user-visible `Retry sync` action exists on the existing Settings/Account/Sync-status surface, re-arms eligible temporary failures, requests the same unique sync pipeline and preserves idempotency; the app is not redesigned.

The persisted Room outbox is the authority for pending work and survives repository recreation, worker recreation and application process reconstruction; no in-memory-only pending-mutation authority exists. This is proven deterministically.
AUTH_REQUIRED preserves Room rows, the outbox, conflict records and the checkpoint; a later sign-in resumes work.
Network-required work resumes when connectivity returns, using WorkManager constraints and the existing unique pipeline; no FCM, no push provider, no permanent background socket.

A sync trigger that arrives while sync work is already running is not silently lost: the smallest correct mechanism is chosen with deterministic evidence against the actual WorkManager version and ExistingWorkPolicy, and the test TRIGGER_DURING_ACTIVE_SYNC proves that all work is eventually observed/applied, that no mutation is applied twice and that exactly one serialized pipeline exists.

Safe minimal outbox coalescing avoids sending many obsolete UPDATE mutations for the same entity when a later mutation supersedes them, without breaking CREATE, DELETE, Trash, revision semantics or mutation idempotency; unclear combinations are not coalesced; the rules are deterministic and tested.

Conflicts are represented by a persisted record that survives process death, carrying at minimum accountId, entity type, entity client UUID, conflict type, local state/payload, remote/server state/payload, local/base revision, server/current revision, createdAt and resolution state; no secrets are stored and no generic giant event system is created.

A stale baseRevision remains HTTP 409 REVISION_CONFLICT, and the response carries enough authoritative server state/revision for the client to resolve the conflict without relying on a client wall clock; the server remains revision/order authority.
A concurrent title/body conflict is surfaced as an explicit conflict and never silently overwrites text, offering exactly KEEP_LOCAL, KEEP_SERVER and KEEP_BOTH.

KEEP_BOTH keeps the authoritative server version on the original entity and creates a SECOND logical local note from the user's local conflicting content, with a NEW client UUID, the same accountId, SYNC_PENDING and a CREATE mutation in the outbox — never reusing the original client UUID or the original server revision identity.

Checklist conflicts use the existing stable item UUIDs: concurrent additions both survive, different items merge independently, a same-item text conflict is resolved by the server-accepted revision/order (never the client wall clock), and deletion-vs-edit of the same item is explicit and non-silent; no CRDT is introduced.
Label membership uses operation semantics ordered by the server-accepted revision/order; a later accepted remove is not resurrected by replaying an older add, proven by a deterministic test.

Metadata (archive, pin, colour, Trash state) resolves by last-server-accepted ordering using the server revision / server change order; an unsynchronized client updatedAt is never the conflict authority; title/body stay explicitly user-resolved.

Delete-vs-edit is explicit (ACCEPT_DELETE or RESTORE_LOCAL / equivalent names): no silent resurrection, no silent discard of local edited content; RESTORE_LOCAL creates or rebases a valid mutation against the current server state without reusing invalid deletion state, and uses a NEW client UUID where restoration means a logically new note.

TRASH_RETENTION is 7 days (D-06): a note entering Trash carries a Trash timestamp, restoring clears/invalidates the Trash expiry, LOCAL_ONLY notes may use local time, and account-scoped synced notes use the authoritative server-accepted Trash time.

A note trashed offline appears locally in Trash immediately but is never automatically final-deleted until the server has accepted the Trash state; after the authoritative 7-day expiry FINAL_DELETE is enqueued/performed and produces the normal tombstone path.

Trash stays structurally distinct from the sync tombstone; TOMBSTONE_GC is DISABLED; no permanent tombstone retention duration is chosen; no tombstone is garbage-collected merely for being older than 7 days.
Anti-resurrection holds: after a final delete a tombstone exists, and an old mutation or a stale delta/replay cannot make the note reappear.
A remote 404 never silently deletes a live local note; A6 may convert it into a resolvable/non-destructive failure state with no data loss.

Verification is ONE pass after A5 and A6: the backend gate and the Android gate each run once, a failure fixes only the failed path and re-runs only the failed task, the frozen inputs re-hash byte-identical, the scope scan shows changes only inside allowed_paths, the secret scan is clean, and PASS means STOP. No device, no cloud provisioning, no A7+ work.

tasks.done_when: The persisted Room outbox is the only pending-mutation authority; the smallest correct lost-wakeup mechanism is implemented and recorded as an implementation decision with its evidence (the actual WorkManager version and ExistingWorkPolicy are inspected first, and KEEP is neither blindly preserved nor blindly replaced); reconnect uses constraints and the existing unique pipeline; coalescing is deterministic, tested and correctness-preserving; no parallel sync pipeline exists.

tasks.goal: A5 light checkpoint — record the checkpoint state and continue directly to A6. This is a checkpoint, not a stop and not a review.
tasks.boundary: Reporting only. No new contract, no review, no session stop, no Milestone gate.
tasks.verification: A short checkpoint record states BOUNDED_RETRY: READY, MANUAL_RETRY: READY, OUTBOX_DURABLE: READY, LOST_WAKEUP: PROTECTED, AUTH_REQUIRED_PRESERVES_OUTBOX: YES, A5_CHECKPOINT: READY_FOR_A6.
tasks.done_when: The A5 checkpoint is recorded and the session continues directly into A6 without running the Milestone gate.

tasks.goal: A6: the persisted conflict record, the backend authoritative conflict response, and the non-UI conflict-application paths (title/body, checklist, label, metadata, delete-vs-edit, 404 non-destructive).
tasks.boundary: Only KeepLab-Relay/backend/** and the enumerated Android data/DI/test surface. No CRDT, no automatic three-way text merge, no attachments.
tasks.verification: Deterministic tests: a stale baseRevision produces 409 REVISION_CONFLICT carrying the current authoritative revision and the current server payload; the conflict record is persisted with every required field and survives a simulated process reconstruction; a title/body divergence is an explicit conflict and the local text is not overwritten; concurrent checklist additions both survive and different items merge independently; a same-item conflict resolves by server order; a later accepted label remove is not resurrected by an older add; metadata resolves by server order and never by client updatedAt; delete-vs-edit and 404 are non-destructive.
tasks.done_when: A persisted conflict record exists with the required minimum fields and no secrets; the 409 response carries enough authoritative state to resolve; every conflict class has a deterministic, non-silent outcome; no CRDT and no automatic text merge exists.

tasks.goal: A6: the minimal conflict-resolution surface — conflict indicator, resolution screen/dialog, Keep Local, Keep Server, Keep Both (with a NEW client UUID) and delete-vs-edit resolution.
tasks.boundary: The enumerated Android surface including the new ui/conflict package. Tiny integration points only elsewhere; no redesign of Home, theme, navigation architecture or the note editor.
tasks.verification: Deterministic JVM tests over the resolution entry points: KEEP_LOCAL preserves local title/body, rebases against the current server revision, enqueues a new mutation in the current account scope; KEEP_SERVER accepts the server version, updates Room and clears the conflict safely; KEEP_BOTH leaves the server version on the original entity, creates a second logical note with a NEW client UUID and a CREATE mutation in the same account and never reuses the original UUID/revision identity; ACCEPT_DELETE and RESTORE_LOCAL are both reachable and neither silently discards content; the conflict indicator is driven by persisted state.
tasks.done_when: The three title/body choices and the two delete-vs-edit outcomes exist and are exercised; KEEP_BOTH provably creates a new client UUID and a CREATE mutation; the conflict indicator is visible; Home, the theme, the navigation architecture and the note editor are not redesigned.

tasks.goal: A6: 7-day product Trash retention distinct from the sync tombstone, Trash restore, offline-Trash safety, FINAL_DELETE eligibility, TOMBSTONE_GC disabled and tombstone anti-resurrection.
tasks.boundary: The enumerated Android surface. No account deletion, no attachments, no tombstone GC.
tasks.verification: Deterministic tests: trashing writes a Trash timestamp; Trash != tombstone (trashing never writes deletedAt); restoring before 7 days clears the expiry and restores the note; 7-day eligibility yields FINAL_DELETE and the normal tombstone path; an offline, unacknowledged client Trash timestamp never causes a permanent deletion; after a final delete a tombstone exists and an old mutation or stale delta replay cannot resurrect the note; no code path garbage-collects a tombstone by age.
tasks.done_when: TRASH_RETENTION = 7 DAYS is implemented with a Trash timestamp and restore invalidation; the authoritative server-accepted Trash time governs account-scoped notes; FINAL_DELETE produces the normal tombstone path; TOMBSTONE_GC is disabled; no tombstone retention duration is chosen anywhere; anti-resurrection holds.

tasks.goal: A6 backend: the conflict response payload, Trash timestamp, final-delete/tombstone handling and change-log semantics, only as required by M3.
tasks.boundary: Only KeepLab-Relay/backend/**. No attachments, no object storage, no collaboration, no multi-device feature, no push.
tasks.verification: Deterministic backend tests: a stale baseRevision returns 409 with the current authoritative revision and current server payload; the server revision and change-log order remain the only ordering authority; a Trash state change carries a server-accepted Trash timestamp; a final delete writes a tombstone and the tombstone is never auto-purged; a stale/duplicate mutation still cannot double-apply or resurrect a tombstoned entity; new migrations exist only if genuinely needed and contain nothing beyond M3.
tasks.done_when: The 409 response carries enough authoritative state to resolve; Trash timestamp handling and final-delete/tombstone handling exist as M3 requires; the atomic dedupe/apply/revision/change-log consistency boundary is unchanged; no attachments, collaboration, multi-device or push code exists; the transactional semantics are not weakened by the absence of a live PostgreSQL.

tasks.goal: The single Milestone verification pass, the scope/secret scans and the M3 report.

Android: cd /mnt/AndroidDev/Projects/KeepLab-Relay && ./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug (ONCE). stop_conditions: Any required write falls outside allowed_paths or targets a forbidden path: STOP and emit CONTRACT_DEVIATION.
Any frozen_inputs file has drifted: STOP and emit STALE_M3_INPUT.

The independent backend project cannot work without changing a repository-root Gradle file, or the Android side needs a change to settings.gradle.kts / build.gradle.kts / gradle.properties / the wrapper: STOP and emit M3_ROOT_GRADLE_CHANGE_REQUIRED with the exact file and change; do not make the change.

A needed Android change falls outside the enumerated surface (for example a theme, a shared UI widget, a resource file, androidTest, benchmark or a Room schema export): STOP and emit M3_SURFACE_BROADENING_REQUIRED with the exact file and reason; do not broaden silently.
Any account deletion would have to be implemented: STOP — D-05 is pending and account deletion is out of scope.
Any attachment, binary upload/download, object storage, sharing or collaboration feature would be needed: STOP.
Multi-device hardening or multi-account would be needed: STOP — A8/A9.
A push provider, FCM or a background push architecture would be needed: STOP.
A CRDT or an automatic three-way text merge would be needed: STOP — those are not adopted.

A permanent tombstone retention duration would have to be chosen, or a tombstone would have to be garbage-collected by age: STOP — SYNC_TOMBSTONE_RETENTION_OR_COMPACTION is a separate, unmade decision.
A tombstone GC/compaction mechanism would have to be implemented: STOP — TOMBSTONE_GC is DISABLED for M3.
Account-scoped offline Trash would be final-deleted on an unacknowledged client timestamp alone: STOP — that is a data-loss path.
A note would have to be resurrected, or a concurrent title/body conflict silently overwritten: STOP.
The Android device would have to be touched, or adb, Maestro, UiAutomator, an instrumentation run or an APK install used: STOP; M3 is device-free.
Any cloud resource would have to be provisioned, any cloud credential used, or any production deployment performed: STOP.
Docker, podman or PostgreSQL would have to be installed to proceed: STOP — record LIVE_POSTGRES_INTEGRATION = SKIPPED_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE and use deterministic tests.
A real secret would have to be written, committed or echoed into evidence, or a token/password/OTP/refresh secret logged: STOP.
Hermes configuration, the hook allowlist, Hermes core, contract_guard.py, the frozen P0B-CLOSE contract, an A0/A1/A2/M2 package or this package would have to be modified: STOP.
The contract package manifest does not verify: STOP.
The M3 session would have to broaden its own allowed paths: STOP; a new human-approved contract is required.
The session is about to stop after A5: STOP — A5 is a checkpoint, not a stop; continue directly to A6.
An A5 contract, an A6 contract, an A5/A6 review, a post-PASS audit or a separate D-06 governance task is being created: STOP — one milestone contract, one session, one verification pass.
A7, A8 or A9 work is being started: STOP.
A gate fails and the fix would reach outside allowed_paths: STOP.
The same failure survives two genuine fixes: STOP and perform ONE root-cause analysis; do not restart M3 from zero.
More than roughly 30 tool calls have occurred before meaningful product writes without a real blocker: STOP overhead work and execute (PROCESS_OVERHEAD_TOO_HIGH).
A minor wording, naming or warning issue is being turned into a new contract: STOP — append it compactly to reports/KEEPLAB-MINOR-BACKLOG.md instead.

failure_rule.rule: Read the failure once, fix the failed path only, rerun only the failed task. Do not restart M3 and do not re-run tasks that already passed.
failure_rule.repeated_failure: If the same failure survives two genuine fixes: emit REPEATED_FAILURE and perform one root-cause analysis.
failure_rule.allowed_patch_surface: Only files inside allowed_paths may be edited to fix a failure. A fix that would need a root Gradle change, a forbidden Android file or a new dependency outside the backend/Android dependency surface is a STOP, not a workaround.
failure_rule.gate_rule: Do not re-run the already-passed gate side. A backend failure never justifies re-running the Android gate, and an Android failure never justifies re-running the backend gate.

overhead_rule.statement: M3 is a large milestone and implementation may naturally take time, but process overhead must not dominate.
overhead_rule.rule: After contract activation, the stale-input check and one targeted discovery pass, begin implementation immediately. If process-only work dominates implementation: PROCESS_OVERHEAD_TOO_HIGH — simplify and execute.

decisions.statement: M3 is executed as ONE milestone with ONE contract, ONE execution session and ONE final verification pass: A5 -> A5 light checkpoint -> A6 -> verify once. Phases are checkpoints, not bureaucratic stops.
decisions.rationale: Separate A5/A6 contracts, reviews and post-PASS audits add overhead without adding a verifiable outcome, and the human directive explicitly forbids them.

decisions.statement: D-06 = TRASH_RETENTION_7_DAYS is frozen from HUMAN_PROJECT_OWNER_APPROVAL, 2026-10-06 and recorded in reports/KEEPLAB-M3-HUMAN-DECISIONS.md. SYNC_TOMBSTONE_RETENTION_OR_COMPACTION stays a separate IMPLEMENTATION_DECISION_PENDING concern; the two are never conflated, no permanent tombstone retention duration is chosen, and TOMBSTONE_GC is DISABLED for M3.
decisions.rationale: The human directive freezes the product Trash duration and explicitly forbids reading it as a sync-tombstone retention and forbids GC'ing tombstones for age.

decisions.statement: The Android write surface is enumerated, not the whole app: the data/di/model packages, one new ui/conflict package, the sync-status/conflict/Trash UI packages, the application/activity entry points, AndroidManifest.xml, app/build.gradle.kts, gradle/libs.versions.toml and app/src/test/**.
decisions.rationale: A5 and A6 genuinely need those surfaces; themes, shared widgets, resources, androidTest, benchmark and schemas are provably unrelated and stay blocked.

decisions.statement: The root Android Gradle surface is unchanged; only app/build.gradle.kts and gradle/libs.versions.toml may change, and only to add dependencies M3 genuinely needs (for example a WorkManager test artifact). ROOT_GRADLE_CHANGE: NO.
decisions.rationale: A test/runtime dependency addition is an ordinary module-level change. Nothing M3 needs justifies touching settings.gradle.kts, the root build file, gradle.properties or the wrapper.

decisions.statement: Bounded retry is implemented with the smallest correct mechanism on the existing architecture. Recorded implementation decisions: AUTO_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5 per outbox mutation (the durable bound; matches STATE-MODEL §2 'attempts exhausted (e.g. 5)'); BACKOFF_POLICY = EXPONENTIAL (WorkManager BackoffPolicy.EXPONENTIAL for the run, plus a durable per-mutation attemptCount bound); BACKOFF_INITIAL_DELAY = 30 seconds; BACKOFF_MAX_DELAY = 5 hours (WorkManager's own exponential cap). The executor may adjust a constant if deterministic evidence requires it and must record the final values; it must not remove the bound.
decisions.rationale: The directive asks for a small bounded policy with simple constants chosen from the current architecture, and forbids marking temporary conditions permanent by default. The existing outbox already carries attemptCount and lastErrorCode, so the durable bound needs no new authority.

decisions.statement: Manual retry is one user-visible `Retry sync` action on the existing Settings/Account/Sync-status surface; it re-arms eligible temporary failures and requests the same unique `note_sync` pipeline, preserving idempotency (the outbox mutationId stays the idempotency key). No app redesign.
decisions.rationale: The directive requires one simple user-visible retry action preferring the existing sync-status surface and forbids redesigning the app.

decisions.statement: The persisted Room outbox is the only pending-mutation authority. No in-memory-only pending state may exist. Durability is proven by deterministic simulation: persist Room state, destroy/recreate the repository and sync objects, resume from the persisted outbox/checkpoint.
decisions.rationale: The directive requires outbox durability across repository/worker/process reconstruction and forbids an in-memory-only authority; true device process death is explicitly not required for M3.

decisions.statement: Lost-wakeup protection is an A5 implementation decision, not a frozen choice. The executor inspects the actual WorkManager version (androidx.work 2.10.5) and the current ExistingWorkPolicy, then selects the smallest correct mechanism (allowed examples: persistent request generation + drain-until-stable; serialized append/rerun; a deterministic equivalent), records it, and proves it with the TRIGGER_DURING_ACTIVE_SYNC test: all work eventually observed/applied, no duplicate mutation apply, exactly one serialized pipeline. ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP is neither blindly preserved nor blindly replaced.
decisions.rationale: The directive forbids both blind preservation and blind change, requires evaluating the real WorkManager version, and forbids parallel sync pipelines.

decisions.statement: Reconnect resumption uses WorkManager constraints and the existing unique pipeline only: no FCM, no push provider, no permanent background socket.
decisions.rationale: The directive prohibits a push architecture in M3 and the frozen architecture already specifies NetworkType.CONNECTED on the unique pipeline.

decisions.statement: Outbox coalescing is safe and minimal: it only collapses an obsolete UPDATE superseded by a later mutation for the same entity, and it must preserve CREATE, DELETE, Trash, revision semantics and mutation idempotency. An unclear combination is NOT coalesced. The rules are deterministic and tested. Correctness > optimization.
decisions.rationale: The directive requires minimal safe coalescing and states that correctness outranks the optimization.

decisions.statement: Conflicts are persisted in Room as a first-class record carrying accountId, entity type, entity client UUID, conflict type, local payload, remote/server payload, local/base revision, server/current revision, createdAt and resolution state. No secrets are stored and no generic event system is built.
decisions.rationale: The directive requires conflicts to survive process death with that minimum information, and explicitly forbids a generic giant event system and secret storage.

decisions.statement: The backend 409 REVISION_CONFLICT response is extended to carry the current authoritative revision and the current server payload for the entity, so a client can resolve without a client wall clock. The server remains the single revision/order authority.
decisions.rationale: The directive requires enough authoritative server state/revision to resolve the conflict, and forbids relying on the client wall clock.

decisions.statement: Title/body conflicts are explicitly user-resolved with exactly KEEP_LOCAL, KEEP_SERVER and KEEP_BOTH. KEEP_LOCAL preserves local text, rebases against the current server revision, enqueues a new mutation and uses the current account scope. KEEP_SERVER accepts the authoritative server version, updates Room and clears the conflict safely. KEEP_BOTH leaves the authoritative server version on the original note and creates a SECOND logical local note (NEW client UUID, new local identity as appropriate, same accountId, SYNC_PENDING, CREATE mutation) without reusing the original client UUID or server revision identity.
decisions.rationale: The directive specifies exactly these three outcomes and the new-UUID requirement for KEEP_BOTH.

decisions.statement: Checklist conflicts use the existing stable item UUIDs: concurrent additions both survive, different items merge independently, a same-item conflict resolves by the server-accepted revision/order (never the client wall clock), and deletion-vs-edit of the same item is explicit/non-silent. No CRDT is introduced.
decisions.rationale: The directive specifies exactly this behaviour and explicitly forbids introducing a CRDT.

decisions.statement: Label membership uses operation semantics ordered by the server-accepted revision/order; a later accepted remove is never resurrected by replaying an older add, proven deterministically.
decisions.rationale: SYNC-DEC-012/013 and the directive require operation semantics rather than a set union, with server order as the authority.

decisions.statement: Metadata (archive, pin, colour, Trash state) resolves by last-server-accepted ordering using the server revision / server change order; an unsynchronized client updatedAt is never the conflict authority. Title/body remain explicit user-resolved conflicts.
decisions.rationale: SYNC-DEC-011 and the directive: a single global LWW on client timestamps would silently lose data.

decisions.statement: Delete-vs-edit is explicit with ACCEPT_DELETE and RESTORE_LOCAL (equivalent names allowed). No silent resurrection and no silent discard of local edited content. RESTORE_LOCAL creates/rebases a valid mutation against the current server state without reusing invalid deletion state, and uses a NEW client UUID where restoration means a logically new note.
decisions.rationale: The directive requires an explicit, represented conflict with those two minimum outcomes.

decisions.statement: TRASH_RETENTION = 7 DAYS. A note entering Trash carries a Trash timestamp (a new local column is required; NoteEntity currently has none). Restoring clears/invalidates the Trash expiry. LOCAL_ONLY notes may use local time; account-scoped synced notes use the authoritative server-accepted Trash time. A note trashed offline appears locally in Trash immediately but is not automatically final-deleted until the server accepted the Trash state; after the authoritative 7-day expiry FINAL_DELETE is enqueued/performed and produces the normal tombstone path.
decisions.rationale: D-06 plus the directive's explicit offline-Trash safety rule, which exists to prevent a client-only timestamp from causing permanent data loss.

decisions.statement: Trash is structurally distinct from the sync tombstone; TOMBSTONE_GC is DISABLED; no permanent tombstone retention duration is chosen; no tombstone is garbage-collected merely for being older than 7 days. Tombstone compaction is a future Milestone decision requiring an anti-resurrection protocol.
decisions.rationale: The directive freezes this posture and forbids the 7-day coupling.

decisions.statement: A remote 404 never deletes a live local note; it is a NOT_FOUND_NON_DESTRUCTIVE state that may be converted into a resolvable/non-destructive failure state. A final delete never resurrects.
decisions.rationale: INVARIANT ERR-3 and the directive's non-destructive 404 rule, which stays in force in M3.

decisions.statement: The error/retry classification is one small explicit enumeration: AUTH_REQUIRED, CONFLICT, TEMPORARY_RETRYABLE, PERMANENT_VALIDATION_FAILURE, NOT_FOUND_NON_DESTRUCTIVE, SUCCESS. A generic 5xx is TEMPORARY_RETRYABLE and never permanent by default.
decisions.rationale: The directive requires the small explicit classification and forbids treating a generic 5xx as permanent.

decisions.statement: Room moves directly to the next clean schema version by an experimental bump with DEV_DATABASE_RESET_REQUIRED = YES when M3 needs new local structures (the persisted conflict record, the Trash timestamp, the outbox retry fields); no migration chain is authored. The backend gains new migrations only as M3 requires, with no production compatibility chain.
decisions.rationale: Project data is disposable experimental data (CLEAN_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE > PRESERVE_TEST_DATA).

decisions.statement: M3 is device-free and cloud-free: no adb, no Maestro, no UiAutomator, no APK install, no cloud provisioning, no infrastructure installation; a live-PostgreSQL check is optional and its absence is recorded as SKIPPED_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE without weakening the transactional semantics.
decisions.rationale: The directive makes M3 device-free by default and forbids installing infrastructure inside M3.

decisions.statement: Verification is ONE pass with both gates run once each; a failure fixes the failed path and re-runs only the failed task; a repeated failure triggers ONE root-cause analysis; PASS means STOP.
decisions.rationale: Milestone execution: no review of review, no post-PASS audit, no re-run of a passing task.
